meta.title: Kite codex
meta.description: Every airframe in Layangin, with the aerodynamic numbers behind it: sail area, mass, lift and drag coefficients, tail drag and handling.

header.title: The rack
header.lead: Eight airframes. The shape is the stat sheet — sail area, mass and tail drag are what make one kite steady and another quick.

tooltip.area: Larger sails generate more lift and more drag. Both scale with area.
tooltip.mass: Heavier kites resist gusts but sink faster in light wind.
tooltip.lift: Peak lift coefficient of the sail. Higher means more pull for the same wind.
tooltip.drag: Baseline resistance through the air, before tails.
tooltip.tailDrag: Extra drag from the tails. High tail drag means very stable and slow to steer.
tooltip.agility: How quickly the sail answers your steering.
tooltip.stability: How strongly the kite returns to trim after being upset.
tooltip.lineStrength: How well the line resists being worn through.
tooltip.cutPower: How fast this rig wears through the other line.

pecut.name: Pecut
pecut.lore: The plain fighting diamond. Two bamboo spars, a paper sail, and nothing else — the kite almost everyone learns on, and still a fair fight in the right hands.

delta.name: Delta
delta.lore: A modern triangle with a keel instead of a tail. Very quick to the crossing and very quick to over-rotate; there is no tail to save you.

bebean.name: Bebean
bebean.lore: The Balinese fish. A broad sail that hangs on in light air and simply will not come down, at the cost of answering the line slowly.

kotak.name: Box kite
kotak.lore: Two cells and no tail at all. The steadiest thing in the sky and the hardest to steer — it wins by outlasting, not by cutting.

sawangan.name: Sawangan
sawangan.lore: The big bowed kite with a humming bow across the top. You hear it before you see it. Heavy, relentless, and hard on your own arms.

elang.name: Elang
elang.lore: Swept wings and a sharp edge. Fast, light and unforgiving — it bites hard but has little line to spare if the exchange goes the wrong way.

janggan.name: Janggan
janggan.lore: The Balinese dragon: a small crowned sail dragging a tail many times its own length. The tail is the kite. Nothing upsets it, and nothing hurries it.

naga.name: Naga Senja
naga.lore: The dusk dragon's own rig, jagged and triple-tailed. The best of everything on the rack, and priced accordingly.

wajik.name: Wajik
wajik.lore: Named for the diamond-cut rice cake. The plainest shape on the rack and the cheapest to rebuild after a bad afternoon.

ketupat.name: Ketupat
ketupat.lore: A squarer diamond with one long ribbon. Slower to answer the line than a pecut, and steadier for it.

daun.name: Daun
daun.lore: Leaf-shaped, rounded at the shoulders. Holds air well in a light breeze and dislikes being hurried.

panji.name: Panji
panji.lore: A banner kite: narrow, tall, and dragging a long ribbon. Very stable, very slow.

sirip.name: Sirip
sirip.lore: A bare fin with no tail at all. Quick and slippery, and it will drop the moment you stall it.

gapangan.name: Gapangan
gapangan.lore: The low-waisted village diamond. The bulk sits below the spar, which is what keeps it pointing up.

pethetan.name: Pethetan
pethetan.lore: Small, narrow and light. Almost nothing to it, which is exactly why beginners can fly one.

aduan.name: Aduan
aduan.lore: Stripped for fighting: no tails, no decoration, nothing to slow it into a crossing.

koang.name: Koang
koang.lore: The owl. Swept wings and a notched tail; it turns faster than it looks like it should.

kupu.name: Kupu
kupu.lore: Butterfly wings, pinched at the waist. Wide and showy, and surprisingly hard to upset.

capung.name: Capung
capung.lore: Dragonfly: four thin arms and a long streamer. Almost all span, almost no area.

rokkaku.name: Rokkaku
rokkaku.lore: The six-sided Japanese fighter, bowed across two spars. Steady, strong-pulling, hard to move.

bulan.name: Bulan
bulan.lore: A crescent with horns reaching back past the middle. The concave trailing edge sheds air unevenly and it wanders.

tameng.name: Tameng
tameng.lore: Flat-topped like a shield, with straight flanks. Presents a lot of sail to a gust.

lampion.name: Lampion
lampion.lore: Barrel-shaped, flat at both ends, braced with extra spars. Boxy and solid.

terbang.name: Ikan Terbang
terbang.lore: Flying fish: a broad belly and a deeply forked tail that streams behind it.

gasing.name: Gasing
gasing.lore: Eight-sided like a spinning top. Compact, dense, and it holds a line angle well.

kembang.name: Kembang
kembang.lore: A six-petal flower. All those points shed vortices, which costs speed and buys stability.

pari.name: Pari
pari.lore: Manta ray. An enormous span on a shallow chord — the most efficient lifting sail on the rack.

kelelawar.name: Kelelawar
kelelawar.lore: Bat wings, swept hard back with a deep notch. Fast into a crossing and twitchy once there.

hiu.name: Hiu
hiu.lore: Shark: narrow, deep-bodied, one heavy tail. Cuts a very clean line through the air.

keris.name: Keris
keris.lore: Barbed like the blade. The flared tips make it bite into a crossing at an angle.

tombak.name: Tombak
tombak.lore: A spear: almost no span, all length. Slices upwind better than anything else here.

sendaren.name: Sendaren
sendaren.lore: Carries a humming bow that you hear before you see the kite. Heavy, and it pulls all afternoon.

wau-bulan.name: Wau Bulan
wau-bulan.lore: The bowed moon kite. A huge crescent sail on a hummer — loud in every sense.

dandang.name: Dandang
dandang.lore: A big bowed barrel with three spars. Built to hang in the sky and refuse to move.

kepiting.name: Kepiting
kepiting.lore: Crab: four stubby arms and two side tassels. Ugly, wide, and hard to knock down.

bintang-laut.name: Bintang Laut
bintang-laut.lore: Five thick points. The deep notches make it slow, and slow is sometimes what wins.

merak.name: Merak
merak.lore: Peacock: two lobes each side and a tail that runs for metres. Spectacular and immovable.

garuda.name: Garuda
garuda.lore: Broad swept wings and a forked tail. The most balanced airframe above the rare tier.

gurita.name: Gurita
gurita.lore: Octopus: a ragged trailing edge trailing three arms. All that drag makes it painfully steady.

mahkota.name: Mahkota
mahkota.lore: A seven-point crown with a long ribbon. Flown at festivals more than in duels — but it duels well.

kalajengking.name: Kalajengking
kalajengking.lore: Scorpion: barbed sail, single dragon tail four metres long. The tail is the weapon.

sayap.name: Sayap
sayap.lore: Pure wing. The widest span and the shallowest chord here — enormous lift, no forgiveness.

wau-kucing.name: Wau Kucing
wau-kucing.lore: The bowed cat kite, nearly two metres across with a ribbon to match.

taring.name: Taring
taring.lore: Fang: narrow, jagged, and fitted with the sharpest gelasan money buys.

matahari.name: Matahari
matahari.lore: Twelve points around a full circle. Absurd, unmistakable, and genuinely very hard to cut.

puyuh.name: Angin Puyuh
puyuh.lore: Whirlwind: ten ragged tongues and a five-metre dragon tail. Turns like a barge, cuts like a saw.

jangkar.name: Jangkar
jangkar.lore: Anchor: a cross sail with three tails. Built entirely around not being moved.

tapak.name: Tapak Naga
tapak.lore: Bowed, four-lobed, dragging four and a half metres of tail. A festival kite that fights.

kanggokan.name: Kanggokan
kanggokan.lore: Three spars, a hummer, and three tails. The heaviest thing anyone sensibly flies.

sultan.name: Sultan Langit
sultan.lore: The largest airframe here: swept wings, a bow, and five and a half metres of dragon tail.

picker.title: Pick your kite
picker.note: Each cell is a different airframe — a different shape with different numbers behind it. The livery and colourway come from the shop and apply to whichever shape you fly.
